title: The Red Eye Emergency

patient.name: Mdm Lee Siew Poh
patient.presenting_complaint: Sudden severe pain in the right eye with blurred vision and vomiting, started 2 hours ago

history.hpc: Mdm Lee presents to SNEC OPD with sudden onset severe right eye pain. She says it came on about 2 hours ago while she was watching TV. The pain is very bad — she rates it 9/10. She also has nausea and has vomited once. She notices the vision in her right eye is very blurry, like looking through fog. She has never had this before.
history.pmhx: Hypertension on medication. No previous eye surgery or eye conditions.
history.social_hx: Lives alone. Daughter brought her in today.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: mid-dilated fixed pupil, corneal haze/oedema, conjunctival redness. Left eye: normal.
examination_findings.fundus: Unable to assess right fundus due to corneal oedema

investigations.iop_nct: RE: 58 mmHg. NCT reading taken after patient settled — multiple readings consistent.
investigations.va_distance: RE: CF at 1m (unable to read logMAR chart). LE: 6/9 on LogMAR chart.

diagnosis: Acute Angle Closure Glaucoma (AACG) — right eye. Category 1 emergency. Must be seen by doctor within 10 minutes.

immediate: Triage as Category 1 — see doctor within 10 minutes
Alert doctor immediately to the patient's condition
Document triage time, presenting complaint, and vital signs on SNEC Triage Form
Do NOT instil any drops without doctor's order
follow_up: Doctor will manage acute IOP reduction
Prepare for possible laser iridotomy or IV acetazolamide
Monitor patient closely while waiting for doctor
patient_education: Reassure patient that help is coming
Advise patient not to rub her eye
Keep patient calm and in a comfortable seated position

key_points: Asks about onset and duration of pain (sudden, 2 hours)
Asks about severity and nature of pain (very severe, 9/10)
Asks about associated symptoms: nausea/vomiting, blurred vision, haloes around lights
Asks about past eye history and medications
Uses structured history approach: general health → presenting problem → past ocular history
Measures VA in both eyes (affected and unaffected)
Observes and documents anterior segment signs (red eye, cloudy cornea, mid-dilated pupil)
Records findings accurately on triage form
Recognises this as an ocular emergency
Identifies the condition as acute angle closure glaucoma or acute painful red eye with high IOP
Correctly assigns SNEC Triage Category 1 (see doctor within 10 minutes)
Does not instil drops without doctor's order
Completes SNEC Triage Form with all required fields
Documents all findings and triage time
